transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-04-01 10:00 AM PDT
Duration: 47 minutes (approx)
Record: Zoom cloud
Attendees: Avery (Redwood AE), Noah (Redwood SE), Lina (Redwood CSM), Janelle (Verdexa CTO), Diego (Verdexa NetEng), Priya (Verdexa Compliance), Samir (Verdexa SRE)

Summary (auto):
Customer is evaluating Redwood for a private onramp. Primary concerns: regional restrictions for PHI, VPC peering/transit gateway architecture, stable egress / static IPs for allowlisting, KMS integration and audit logs. They want a PoC to validate latency and egress controls.

Topics: VPC peering vs PrivateLink, Transit Gateway architecture, private endpoints, egress IP allocation, regional gating/data residency, SOC2/KMS, A/B for Dedicated vs Private economics

Action items (auto-generated): see action_items metadata above

Transcript body:
[00:00] Avery: hey everyone thanks for joining, um this is Avery from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account. quick intro from me then noah will dig into the topology questions.
[00:18] Janelle: hi, i'm janelle, CTO at verdexa hi all. we're trying to understand how we can run inference on PHI data with minimal blast radius. really key to keep us in our cloud regions.
[00:30] Diego: hey all, diego here. i own networking. main ask — static egress IPs for allowlisting and how you do private endpoints into our VPC.
[00:40] Noah: cool, Noah Rivera, solutions engineer. i'll sketch the typical private onramp patterns and tradeoffs. i'll try to call out latency numbers we've seen for similar setups.
[00:51] Priya: priya — compliance. SOC2 is table stakes; also concerned about key management and audit retention. we need to know if logs can be forwarded to our SIEM.
[01:05] Avery: great, quick agenda: 1) listen to the constraints 2) talk through three topologies we recommend 3) call out region gating and compliance artifacts 4) next steps + action items. sound good?
[01:18] Janelle: yep. go ahead.
[01:22] Noah: ok first pattern — service endpoint inside customer VPC using PrivateLink/private endpoints. basically we deploy a private connector in your VPC that terminates to Redwood's private control plane. this keeps egress minimal, and traffic never hits public internet.
[01:41] Diego: are you talking about classic aws privatelink or you have your own proxies? we use aws TGW and we try to avoid VPC peering because of scale.
[01:51] Noah: good call — we support both privatelink style endpoints and TGW attachments. for scale we usually recommend using the transit gateway with an appliance VPC in the middle. appliances are what we call the private onramp proxies.
[02:06] Speaker 2: (mumble) right, right
[02:10] Noah: as for egress IPs — we can allocate static egress IP ranges from the appliance VPC and NAT those to your allowlist. if you run dedicated, you can reserve specific Elastic IPs in the customer-managed VPC or we can provide egress via our managed NAT with stable IPs per region.
[02:30] Diego: hm, how many eips are we talking? we need to keep under our firewall quota — currently we allow 10 source IPs per vendor.
[02:40] Noah: for a small PoC you can usually do 2-4 eips per region; for larger deployments we have patterns to squash across fewer IPs using SNAT, but that may increase NAT connection tracking. tradeoff: fewer IPs easier for firewall rules, more NAT state might affect throughput.
[02:58] Priya: question on logs — can you stream audit logs to our cloudwatch or Splunk? basically we need records of model runs with non-PHI metadata.
[03:10] Noah: yes, our private control plane can push audit logs to a customer destination via a forwarder — options: Kinesis/CloudWatch/S3 push or direct syslog to Splunk. retention and schema can be configured, though PHI content shouldn't be present in the logs if configured correctly — we can redact or hash inputs at the agent layer.
[03:32] Janelle: about region constraints: Verdexa must keep PHI in us-east-1 and eu-west-1 only. other regions are blocked. can you gate model execution to those regions?
[03:44] Avery: absolutely — region policy routing is a feature. we can pin model instances to specific regions and enforce routing policy to keep inference in those allowed regions, with fallback blocked or logged.
[03:56] Samir: any cold start latency implications if we limit to two regions only? we expect spikes during business hours.
[04:05] Noah: limiting regions reduces available capacity; you'll need reserved capacity (Dedicated) to meet throughput SLOs for heavy spikes. for PoC we can run hosted-private in customer VPC with modest concurrency; latency numbers we've observed are 60-120ms median token time for short prompts, but for your payloads (long context) it could be higher.
[04:27] Diego: what about KV cache — do you support shared cache across AZs? we need cache locality because we have multi-AZ setup.
[04:36] Noah: we support KV cache replication inside a region; cross-AZ replication is supported, but cross-region cache syncing isn't automatic — we keep caches regional to minimize RTT. so pin workloads to the region where the cache is warm.
[04:55] Janelle: ok interesting. another practical: how do you do key management — can we bring our own KMS?
[05:02] Noah: yes BYOK is supported for Private. you can point to your KMS/HSM; we integrate with customer-managed CMKs for encryption at rest and a separate key for model artifacts. we'll share our KMS integration guide.
[05:14] Priya: are there certifications for the private deployment? we need SOC2 plus encryption attestations.
[05:20] Avery: we have SOC2 reports for our hosted control plane; for private deployments we provide a compliance pack and architecture review. we'll share our SOC2 letter and the private deployment checklist.
[05:32] Diego: firewall rules — do you require specific ports inbound to the appliance? our security team is strict.
[05:40] Noah: minimal inbound: control plane uses HTTPS to the endpoint; for model traffic we keep it inside the VPC. there may be a small set of outbound ports for telemetry; we can provide a hardened allowlist.
[05:51] Janelle: what's the data flow — does raw payload leave our VPC at any point?
[05:57] Noah: with Private mode and privatelink — no. payloads terminate in your VPC to the appliance, processing happens in the private pool we've attached. only metadata (if you opt in) or aggregated metrics might leave unless you choose otherwise. for Dedicated we can run entirely in your tenant with no egress.
[06:20] Avery: quick poll — which is the main priority: 1) no egress at all, 2) low latency for spikes, 3) minimal ops overhead. janelle?
[06:29] Janelle: number 1 is the top, then low latency.
[06:33] Diego: for us it's static IPs and predictable NAT behaviour.
[06:37] Priya: compliance first for us as well.
[06:41] Noah: ok so recommendation: start PoC with PrivateLink + TGW appliance in us-east-1 only, reserve small dedicated capacity if you expect bursty traffic, allocate 2-3 EIPs for PoC and we can compact later. we'll also scope a Dedicated reserved pool if you need guaranteed throughput.
[06:58] Speaker 3: (background) yep
[07:02] Diego: what's the onboarding time and who manages certificates?
[07:06] Avery: onboarding usually 2-4 weeks for Private onramp — depends on network approvals. certificate management: clients can either use our managed certs inside the appliance VPC or bring their own TLS certs if they prefer.
[07:19] Samir: are there any known issues with TGW and route table limits? we already have many attachments.
[07:26] Noah: TGW route table scaling is a known constraint. for large scale we sometimes suggest consolidating attachments into an appliance VPC to reduce per-account route table entries. we'll diagram that for Diego.
[07:40] Janelle: can we run inference in our on-prem data center? we have legacy systems with very low latency requirements for some pipelines.
[07:48] Noah: on-prem is supported via an air-gapped package; it has additional ops overhead. latency would be best if you run inference next to your data center but model updates and monitoring require a control plane handshake — we can run a private control plane in your network.
[08:05] Priya: about audit logs retention — can we ensure logs are immutable for 2 years?
[08:12] Noah: retention is configurable; we can push logs to S3 with WORM-like configuration on the customer side; immutability depends on your bucket policies. we'll add an example for Priya.
[08:24] Avery: wanted to flag cost tradeoffs: Dedicated capacity reduces latency variance and gives predictable unit cost, but requires monthly commitment. Private onramp is more flexible but you pay regional premiums and egress handling costs.
[08:39] Janelle: can you give us ballpark numbers now? even ranges are useful.
[08:44] Avery: rough: hosted low-volume is cheapest per token, Private with TGW and egress IPs adds fixed infra and per-token delta. Dedicated—depends on GPU class; e.g., 32GB A100 or similar, monthly reserved starts in the low tens of thousands for a small reserved pool. we'll follow up with a more detailed pricing sheet.
[09:03] Diego: for firewall change window — we have a Tuesday maintenance slot; do you need downtime to attach the appliance?
[09:11] Noah: usually no downtime; it's an additive attach to TGW or provisioning of privatelink endpoints. we can work in your maintenance window if you prefer to do firewall rule rollout then.
[09:23] Speaker 1: (crosstalk) yeah
[09:28] Priya: encryption in transit — do you support client cert mutual TLS?
[09:33] Noah: mTLS is supported for the control plane endpoints if you require client certs. we can also enable strict TLS with pinned ciphers. we'll include mTLS notes in the architecture doc.
[09:46] Janelle: are there any references from healthcare customers? sometimes we get redacted case studies.
[09:52] Avery: yes we can provide a redacted reference and a checklist from a previous PHI customer — we'll send that after the call.
[10:00] Samir: curious about model pinning/versioning — we need reproducibility for audits. how do rollouts happen in Private?
[10:09] Noah: model version pinning is supported; you can lock endpoints to a model artifact and we support canary rollouts with automatic fallback to prior model if quality regresses. all rollout events are logged.
[10:21] Diego: any constraints on egress bandwidth per appliance? we plan to push about 500 Mbps sustained in peak.
[10:29] Noah: appliances can be sized — for sustained 500Mbps we'd usually recommend multiple instances behind a LB or a larger instance type. we'll size based on concurrency and token-per-second estimates; i'll ask for workload samples from Samir.
[10:44] Janelle: ok, let's talk PoC success criteria: 1) all PHI processing stays in us-east-1, 2) static egress IPs work with our firewall, 3) acceptable latency under 95th pct threshold of X ms.
[10:57] Avery: good criteria. i'll capture that in the follow-up doc.
[11:02] Priya: last question — if we go Dedicated later, is data migration easy?
[11:08] Noah: yes, we support model and KV cache migration; for stateful things we can warm caches into Dedicated instances. there will be a short window of increased I/O but we can orchestrate it.
[11:20] Janelle: timeline — we want to be ready for a pilot by mid-april. is that feasible?
[11:27] Avery: yes, mid April PoC kickoff is doable assuming we get VPC details and TGW info this week.
[11:33] Diego: i'll send the CIDRs and TGW attachment IDs by Friday.
[11:36] Noah: perfect, i'll draft the topology and egress IP plan and share before Monday.
[11:41] Avery: ok let's recap next steps — we'll send architecture deck, compliance docs, pricing sheet, and a proposed PoC plan with timelines. Diego to send network artifacts; Priya will review SOC2 notes.
[11:53] Janelle: thanks everyone.
[11:56] Avery: thanks all — we'll follow up with links.
[12:00] (recording stops)

Shared links discussed: https://redwood.com/docs/private-onramp-architecture (deck), https://redwood.com/compliance/soc2 (SOC2 pack).

End of transcript.
